claims.text: SrTiO3 is a suitable crystalline insulating perovskite for studying lattice thermal conductivity.
Doping SrTiO3 can induce short-range-order precipitates.
Short-range-order precipitates reduce phonon scattering times in SrTiO3.
Reducing phonon scattering times decreases the lattice thermal conductivity of SrTiO3.
High-purity single-crystal SrTiO3 has well-defined lattice vibrations.
The proposed SrTiO3 initial state has a negligible free-carrier contribution to heat transport.
Substituting Sr or Ti with atoms having substantial size or mass mismatch can promote formation of short-range-order precipitates.
Phonon heat transport dominates in the proposed room-temperature to moderately high-temperature regime.
Suitable processing conditions can nucleate and stabilize nanoscale short-range-order precipitates in doped SrTiO3.
Atomic size or mass mismatch between host and dopant atoms produces nanoscale short-range-order precipitates.
Nanoscale short-range-order precipitates act as additional phonon-scattering centers.
Scattering by the precipitates reduces phonon mean free paths.
The doped material will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than undoped SrTiO3.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity reduction depends on the density and distribution of the short-range-order precipitates.
The effect requires a dopant-concentration range that promotes short-range-order precipitation without producing large secondary phases or compromising the crystal structure.
Extreme doping or temperatures that cause other phase transformations may invalidate the predicted behavior.
